content.title: Los Angeles Angels vs New York Yankees Live Stream: How to Watch MLB
content.text: After a wild walk-off win, the New York Yankees go for the series victory on Thursday against the Los Angeles Angels. The New York Yankees go for the series victory in this four-game set when they host the Los Angeles Angels on Thursday afternoon. The Yankees and Angels split the first two games, and New York took the lead in Game 3 on Wednesday with a close 5-4 win in a wild walk-off victory in a game that LA looked like it had locked up. The Yankees are just a half-game back of the AL East-leading Tampa Bay Rays, who have won five straight. The Yankees are 10-8 on the young season and 5-4 at home. Los Angeles is trying to get back to .500 on the season, currently 9-10 overall and 6-7 on the road. The Angels did get good news on Wednesday with DJ Jorge Soler getting a reduced suspension after last week’s brawl when he charged the mound against Reynaldo Lopez. Soler appealed the suspension, and it was reduced from seven games to four. His suspension began on Wednesday and will keep him unavailable for the conclusion of this series or the next against the San Diego Padres. New York will be the big -252 favorite to win this series today in this getaway game. Aaron Judge got the scoring going with a bomb in the first inning on Wednesday, and New York went up 3-0 after two innings, but the Angels took over from there. They did it with three homers from Logan O’Hoppe, Adam Frazier, and Mike Trout. The future Hall of Famer hit a two-run shot in the fifth to put the Angels up 4-3. Los Angeles took that lead into the bottom of the ninth inning. That’s where everything fell apart for the Angels. LA had one out in the bottom of the ninth when Jazz Chisholm Jr. popped up with nobody on base. Shortstop Zach Neto and former Yankee Oswald Peraza had a miscommunication, and the ball dropped between them. Jose Caballero would eventually go on to drive in Chisholm Jr. and Austin Wells on a walk-off two-RBI double. The Yankees will have a great shot at the series victory by starting Max Fried in the finale. The veteran lefty is starting how he left off last season with a 2-0 record and a 1.93 ERA over 28 innings in four starts. The Angels have yet to announce a starter for this finale in an attempt to tie the series. The Angels will host the final series between these two in Anaheim at the beginning of September.
